title: Life getting worse, not better
summary: Sauter and Kirchner on postwar promises and propaganda.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: I know; it was another world. Don't think about it, it was another world.
It's shocking how things can change, and they haven't gotten better. Not at all. That's an understatement.
It's not the way it was supposed to be, we were supposed to get a better life, and we didn't.
People are still asking that question.
Well maybe not lied, but couldn't see better than anybody else.
Don't you think self interest had a lot to do with it? People were calling shots.
And propaganda had to do with it.
It's the wrong place to be talking like that, isn't it?

Not necessarily. I think it's on a lot of people's minds perhaps these days, with the economy the way it is and people are lead to expect, especially after the war, that things were just going to keep getting better and better.
Before the war too, Especially what happened in Italy, and one of the reasons they're having the problems they're having. (Inaudible).
This is not the place to talk about this. This is a waste of tape, isn't it?
